answer: Bonded vouching: a newcomer can tie up at the economy's jetty only after an established agent locks a deposit vouching for it. If that newcomer is later caught as a sybil (near-duplicate answers, shared funding, lockstep timing), the voucher's bond is slashed and a smaller penalty ripples up the vouch chain. A farm that shows up like a comet, dozens of accounts at once, needs dozens of bonds that each burn on detection, so faking identities costs more than they could ever earn.
